svg.title: A single bad row, invisible to code review, caught immediately by a real test
svg.desc: stg_cityflow__trips.sql, reviewed by eye, has nothing wrong with it -- clean SQL, no typos, dbt run succeeds and produces a Postgres view exactly as expected. One row is inserted directly into raw.trips with pickup_zone 9999, a zone that does not exist anywhere in the 265-row zone lookup. dbt run still succeeds -- the view compiles and builds with no error, because nothing about the SQL itself is wrong. Only a relationships test, checking pickup_zone against stg_cityflow__zones's own zone_id column, catches it: Got 1 result, configured to fail if != 0. Neither the code nor dbt run's own success message reveals the problem -- only a test that checks the data itself does.
svg.text: One Bad Row, Invisible to Everything Except a Test
A person reading it has no way to
see that one row's zone doesn't exist.
Also succeeds, with the bad row in it.
dbt run only checks that SQL compiles
and executes -- never what it returns.
One row inserted directly: pickup_zone = 9999, a zone that does not exist
A real dbt test catches it immediately
relationships test: pickup_zone must exist in stg_cityflow__zones
FAIL -- Got 1 result, configured to fail if != 0
the exact test Lesson 2 covers next
